title: Download, and the metadata
idea: Keep the indicator ID and the source link with the numbers.
summary: There is a Download link under every chart on data.un.org. What it gives you carries the identifiers and the provenance that a screenshot loses.

transcript.text: Getting the data out takes one click. What comes with it is the useful part.
Under every chart on the platform there is a Download link. It is easy to miss, and it is on all of them.
Click it and you get the chart's underlying table, ready to copy straight into Excel, Datawrapper or Flourish.
Notice these columns. Entity D C I D and Variable D C I D are the platform's permanent identifiers for the place and the measure. Record them and anyone can reproduce your exact figure.
And these carry the provenance: the unit, and the URL of the agency that published it. This is what makes the file still attributable after it has been forwarded three times.
Copy takes the whole table to your clipboard. Paste it into a spreadsheet and the provenance travels with the numbers.

And here is what actually lands in your spreadsheet. Every single row carries the place, the variable identifier and the year beside the value, so a stray copy-paste cannot separate a number from what it measures.
Keep the identifier and keep the provenance URL. Those two columns are the difference between a spreadsheet and evidence.

deeper.label: Data Finder: a CSV that carries its sources

keep: Keep two columns: Variable DCID (the indicator's permanent ID) and provenanceUrl (the agency's page).
